Subject: Unexpected spike on Feb invoice - urgent

Hi Irene,

We just received our February invoice and there's a ~340% usage spike versus our historical baseline. Invoice attached (optimistai-invoice-feb-2026.pdf). Line items show hosted API tokens - text generation, but we did not run any experiments that could explain this jump.

Can you send a per-route/per-model token breakdown and any evidence of replays/duplicate requests? We need this for internal procurement before we can approve payment.

Quick facts:
- Account: Optimist AI (acct ID 9987)
- Bill date: 2026-02-01 - 2026-02-28
- Observed spike window: 2026-02-05 02:00 UTC through 2026-02-07 05:30 UTC

We'd like to get a resolution/credit or explanation by EOD 2026-02-12 if possible. Happy to hop on a short call.

Thanks,
Aisha
VP of Platform, Optimist AI

Thanks Irene — attached a short excerpt (request_log_excerpt.csv) with timestamps and request ids from the 02/05–02/07 window. Two notes:

- We rolled a tokenizer change in our backend on Feb 4 (migrated a small portion of traffic from tiktoken-v1 to sentencepiece-compat for a new model preprocessor).
- We also deployed a streaming SDK update on Feb 4 that changed how chunking is done; we noticed some client-side retries during that deployment.

We don't have evidence of intentional replays, but there were some 5xx retries from our side 2026-02-05 02:10–02:45 UTC. The logs we attached include duplicated request ids where available.

Appreciate your help. Happy to set up a call if that helps.

Best,
Aisha

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@optimistai.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike on Feb invoice - urgent

Hi Aisha — I've pulled your account metering for the period and cross-checked our ingestion pipeline. Initial findings:

- There are ~14k requests in that window that show multiple identical payload hashes arriving within seconds of each other.
- Our feeder logs show two bursts where the same client nonce was processed 2–3 times; these line up with the 5xx retry timestamps you mentioned.
- Metering appears to have counted each processed request separately (we bill per processed request/token).

Estimate of overcharge: based on comparison to the prior month and removing repeated request hashes, we estimate ~28% of Feb billed tokens are duplicates triggered by client retries and chunked streaming re-encoding. That corresponds to an estimated $3,750 in overage credits.

What I propose:
- Issue a provisional credit of $3,750 against your March invoice while we complete a full forensic (by 2026-02-18).
- Marcus will provide a technical mitigation to prevent double-processing for streaming-chunk re-encodings.

If you'd like, we can escalate this to a payment hold until the credit posts — let me know.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Billing Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@optimistai.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Technical root cause and remediation plan

Hi all — quick technical summary from platform:

Findings:
- The tokenizer migration to sentencepiece-compat increased token counts slightly due to different normalization of whitespace and long punctuation sequences; that explains ~8% of the delta.
- The larger issue (~20% additional tokens) came from a streaming chunk re-encode bug in your SDK where each chunk was re-sent as a new top-level request when a transient 5xx occurred. Our ingestion treats each processed request independently, so duplicates were billed.

Remediation plan (timeline):
- Immediate: Ben to issue provisional credit of $3,750 (manual billing adjustment) — target done by 2026-02-15.
- Short term (this week): We will add idempotency-key checks for streaming-chunked requests server-side, so duplicate chunk replays are deduplicated during metering (target 2026-02-18). This is a non-breaking server-side config change.
- Long term: We will add a tokenization-compatibility note to the docs and a server-side normalization flag you can enable to canonicalize tokens from sentencepiece-style clients (ETA: March release).

If Optimist wants us to hold payment until the full forensic is done, we can accommodate. Otherwise we'll apply the provisional credit and follow up with final numbers after the dedupe run.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
